title: How to Read an Academic Article
summary:
The source is a pedagogical blog post rather than a conventional research paper; it contains no formal abstract, summary section, or author-supplied keywords. Peter G. Klein presents a practical method for reading academic articles efficiently: read the abstract, introduction, and conclusion; skim headings, tables, and figures to identify the article's type and structure; read the full text quickly; then reread the most important parts carefully. After understanding the central argument, readers should assess its consistency and evidentiary support, compare it with related scholarship, examine later works that cite it, and consult broader reference works.

The post has been reused in academic teaching and research-skills materials. It was republished by the International Center for Law & Economics, adapted into a graduate strategy-seminar handout, and assigned as preparatory reading in a university course syllabus. Its recommendations have also been paraphrased or translated in subsequent educational blog posts. These uses indicate influence primarily as an instructional reading strategy rather than as a contribution to a specialized research literature. ([organizationsandmarkets.com](https://organizationsandmarkets.com/2010/08/31/how-to-read-an-academic-article/))
